problems.group: Range Rover Evoque D180 Ingenium Timing Chain Failure
problems.h4: Range Rover Evoque D180 Ingenium Timing Chain Failure - Why 2.0 Diesel Engines Fail Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Oil dilution from incomplete DPF regeneration thins the engine oil, reducing its protective properties. The timing chain tensioner relies on oil pressure - degraded oil causes tensioner failure, leading to chain slack, guide breakage, and eventual chain jump or seizure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain kit, tensioners, guides, and perform full oil system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if caught before chain jumps teeth. Adds 60k+ miles if upgraded parts used

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip cylinder head, replace damaged valves, full timing kit, oil flush
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for engines with minor valve contact but intact block

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value for high-mileage engines. Addresses all failure points permanently

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Range Rover Evoque D180 holds a current UK market value of £8,000-£18,000+ depending on specification and mileage [THIRD-PARTY]. At this valuation, a rebuilt engine replacement cost represents a sensible fraction of the vehicle's total value, making professional replacement highly viable to preserve its premium status.
problems.recommendation: If your D180 has timing chain rattle on cold start but still runs smoothly, invest in a preventative chain replacement at a specialist (£1,200-£1,800). However, if the engine has already jumped timing or lost oil pressure, skip the intermediate repair on a high-mileage Evoque - a rebuilt unit with warranty (£2,500-£4,500) offers better long-term value.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 204DTD Range Rover Evoque D180 engine prices

problems.group: Range Rover Evoque D180 Oil Dilution
problems.h4: Range Rover Evoque D180 Oil Dilution - The Ingenium Diesel Engine Killer
problems.rootCause: Frequent short journeys prevent the DPF from completing active regeneration cycles. Unburned diesel fuel passes into the sump during regeneration attempts, raising oil levels, thinning viscosity, and destroying the oil’s ability to protect bearings, timing components, and turbos.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full oil and filter change (two flushes), DPF static regeneration, PCM software update
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix if underlying driving pattern doesn't change. May last 10-20k miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil pump, timing chain kit, main and big-end bearings, full system flush
repairOptions.longevity: High-risk repair. Damage often extends beyond bearings

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with revised DPF calibration, upgraded oil pump, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if engine has run with heavily diluted oil for extended period or has seized

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Given the £8,000-£18,000+ value band of the Range Rover Evoque D180, replacement is financially sensible if the engine has seized, as repair costs for bottom-end damage frequently approach the vehicle's total value.
problems.recommendation: Oil dilution is a design flaw in the early Ingenium diesel calibration. If your oil level warning appears, act immediately: a specialist oil flush and software update (£250-£400) can prevent catastrophic damage. If the engine has already suffered bottom end knocking, fit a rebuilt unit with the latest engine management calibration.
